fields.description:
## Context / Problem

The sibling admission runner fills fixture coverage once. Two things reopen gaps: a criterion
added to the registry later starts with no fixture, and a criterion whose candidates all failed
to reproduce is left with none. Coverage then decays until someone notices. A repair loop that
spends money unattended needs a bound independent of anyone watching it.

## Approach

**Gap-only scope.** Each run considers only criteria that
`criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')` reports and for which no spec file
exists under `.rebar/evals/` or `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/`. Criteria that already have a
fixture are never revisited, so the loop's work shrinks monotonically to zero — unattended spend
bounded by construction, not by a watchdog.

**Quarantine breaker (a persistent ticket-based quarantine, not an in-memory breaker;** the
sibling a5bf records the pattern). Two triggers file a quarantine ticket titled exactly
`unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>` — the literal prefix `unreliable-criterion: ` (WITH the
trailing space) then the registry criterion id:

1. **Three consecutive failed runs.** The loop persists, per criterion, a consecutive-failure
   counter in its rebar state file (beside the due-stamp). A run fails for a criterion on either
   of two signals, each read from a named sub-step's report: the admission runner's per-criterion
   reproduction-failure result, or the emitter's `FixtureEmitReport.skipped_unbalanced` (no case
   on both sides of the fire/no-fire axis). On the third consecutive such run the loop files the
   ticket. The counter RESETS to zero when the criterion becomes covered or its ticket closes.
2. **Runner-declared un-minable (first-encounter).** The admission runner itself decides a
   criterion cannot be inline-admitted and records a skip-drift entry (`observed="skipped"`)
   with one of its two DISTINCT reasons: `not-inline-admissible` (the ISF class,
   `eval_solver.INLINE_UNADMISSIBLE_CRITERIA = frozenset({'ISF'})`) or
   `container-material-unrecoverable` (the container criteria `CONTAINER_CRITERIA` =
   G3/G4/decomp-shape). These are two reasons, NOT one "not inline-runnable" class — the loop
   does not re-derive inline-runnability; it CONSUMES the runner's verdict. On the first run
   whose drift report carries such an entry for a criterion, it files the ticket immediately, so
   no spend is wasted mining a criterion the runner will not admit.

**How the quarantine feeds the selector — the loop OWNS this wiring; it is NEW work.**
`fixture_selection.select_candidates` does NOT read ticket titles: it skips only criteria in a
caller-supplied `unreliable: dict[criterion_id -> ticket_id]` map (its internal reason string
`unreliable-criterion:{ticket_id}` is keyed on ticket id, a DIFFERENT string from the title).
This loop builds that map: it queries OPEN tickets whose title matches `unreliable-criterion:
<id>`, parses the criterion id, and passes `{id: ticket_id}` to the selector. Creation is
IDEMPOTENT — filed only when no OPEN ticket with that exact title exists — and the map builder
dedupes by criterion id (lowest ticket id wins), so a rare concurrent double-create is
self-healing: the selector still skips the criterion and the extra ticket is a closeable
duplicate. The once-per-interval due-stamp serializes runs.

**Portability.** Recurring work must not depend on a CI provider. The trigger is
operation-linked with an in-process due-stamp: the loop records its last run in the repository's
rebar state, and a rebar plan-review operation advances it once the configured interval
(default 30 days) has elapsed. It is also directly invocable as a command, so an operator, a
cron, or any CI provider can drive it — no step depends on a POSIX-only shell.

**Unattended spend bound + failure disposition.** Mining is free; only admission costs. Each
run pre-flights through `ledger.reserve(..., cap_usd=25.0)` against the loop's own ledger and
stops when remaining headroom cannot cover the next criterion, leaving the rest for the next
interval — bounding unattended spend to $25 per interval however many gaps exist. Because
`finalize()` prices ACTUAL usage, a subsequent `reserve` re-checks cumulative actual spend, so
an actual that overran its estimate makes the NEXT `reserve` raise `BudgetExceeded` (FATAL,
non-retryable): the run stops with already-finalized criteria admitted and their spend
reconciled, and the next interval resumes. A criterion whose candidates fail to reproduce is not
an error — it increments the breaker counter (trigger #1) and the run continues.

## Scope

The loop command, its due-stamp trigger and interval configuration, the per-criterion
consecutive-failure counter, the open-ticket title→`unreliable` map builder that feeds the
selector, both quarantine triggers, the idempotent `unreliable-criterion:` ticket creation, and
the loop's own ledger file. It reuses the sibling selector, emitter and admission runner.

## Non-goals

- Repairing a criterion recorded as unreliable; that is the work the filed ticket represents.
- Revisiting or rewriting a criterion that already has a fixture.
- Any human curation step between mining and admission.

## Compatibility and rollback

Additive: a new command, a new state stamp/counter, and a new ledger file. No existing command,
spec, or persisted format changes. Back-out is deleting the command and its state; nothing reads
it if the command is absent.

## Testing

Unit tests (each named in an AC below) run against a stubbed admission runner over a temporary
store, deterministic without a model; a subprocess test covers the command with no CI
environment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A criterion that already has a spec file is absent from a run's attempt list; `pytest`
      asserts the selected id set excludes it (gap-only scope).
- [x] The third consecutive failed run creates exactly one ticket titled
      `unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>`, and the first and second do not; `pytest` against
      a temporary store asserts the title and the ticket count after each run.
- [x] A `skipped-unbalanced` run (from the emitter) increments the same counter as a runner
      reproduction failure; `pytest` asserts the ticket appears after three mixed-kind runs.
- [x] A criterion with an open ticket of that title is absent from the attempt list; `pytest`
      asserts the id is not selected (the loop's title→`unreliable`-map builder queries the open
      ticket and passes it to `select_candidates`).
- [x] A criterion the runner declares un-minable — a container criterion (drift reason
      `container-material-unrecoverable`) or an ISF-class one (`not-inline-admissible`) — is
      quarantined on FIRST encounter: one ticket filed without three runs; `pytest` asserts the
      ticket exists after a single run over each such seeded criterion.
- [x] Ticket creation is idempotent — a second run while the ticket is open creates no
      duplicate; `pytest` asserts the ticket count stays 1 after a re-run.
- [x] A run stops before a criterion whose estimate exceeds remaining headroom and admits the
      criteria it completed; `pytest` against the real `ledger.reserve` with `cap_usd=25.0`
      asserts the admitted set and that the ledger total is at most 25.0.
- [x] The command runs with no CI environment variables set and reports its attempt list; a
      `pytest` subprocess test with a cleared environment asserts this.
- [x] The due-stamp advances only after the configured interval; `pytest` asserts no attempt at
      interval minus one day and one at the interval.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; a seeded three-failure history produces the
ticket and the selector skip.

## Budget

**Hard cap $100** for building this child and its first runs. Each unattended run is separately
capped at $25 by its own pre-flight; total cost falls to zero once every criterion is covered or
recorded as unreliable.
